include: Reads the contents of another file (a header) in at this point (#include)
#include <cstdio>: C input and output functions such as printf
#include <iostream>: C++ input and output such as cout and cin
#include <vector>: std::vector, an array whose length can change
#include <algorithm>: Common operations such as sort and max
#include <cstring>: C string functions (strlen, strcmp, memset and so on)
#include <cmath>: Math functions (sqrt, pow, fabs and so on)
#include <cstdint>: Integer types with fixed sizes (uint8_t, int32_t and so on)
#include <optional>: std::optional, which expresses whether there is a value
#include <thread>: Threads, and waiting such as sleep_for
#include <chrono>: Lengths of time (milliseconds and so on)
int: The integer type (usually 32 bits, about ±2.1 billion)
unsigned: Makes an integer with no minus values (unsigned)
uint: An unsigned integer (short for unsigned int; used in the Pico SDK and elsewhere)
char: The type for one character (1 byte)
double: The decimal type (double precision, about 15 digits)
float: The decimal type (single precision, about 7 digits). On microcontrollers it is often faster than double
bool: The type for true or false
void: "Nothing". Used for functions with no return value
auto: Lets the compiler decide the type from the right-hand side
constexpr: Makes a constant whose value is decided at build time
static: Inside a function, "a variable that does not disappear between calls"; inside a class, "only one, not one per object"
inline: A hint that the function's body may be expanded where it is called. Used when writing functions in a header
explicit: Stops a constructor from doing type conversions on its own
sizeof: The size of a type or variable (in bytes)
typedef: Gives a type another name (today using is more common)
using: Lets you leave out a namespace name (using namespace std;), or gives a type another name
namespace: A group of names. std is the standard library's namespace
std: The namespace of the C++ standard library (used like std::cout)
main: The function where the program starts
return: Returns the function's answer and ends the function
if: Runs only when the condition is true
else: Runs when the condition is not true
for: Repeats a set number of times. for (initialization; condition; update)
while: Repeats while the condition is true
do: do { } while (condition); a loop that always runs at least once
break: Leaves a loop or a switch
continue: Skips the rest of the loop and goes to the next round
switch: Branches by value. Combined with case
case: One value's case inside a switch (case value:)
default: In a switch, when no case matches
enum: A set of named constants (an enumeration)
struct: A type that bundles data (its members are public from the start)
class: A class (a blueprint bundling data and functions)
public: Can be used from outside the class
private: Can only be used from inside the class
protected: Can be used inside the class and from child classes
this: In a member function, a pointer to "this object itself"
virtual: Makes a function that child classes can override (a virtual function)
override: A marker saying it overrides a parent's virtual function (the compiler catches mistakes)
friend: Shows a class's private parts to a specific function or class
operator: Defines what an operator (such as + or <<) means for your own class
template: Makes a function or class whose type is decided later (a template)
typename: Declares the name of a template's type (template <typename T>)
new: Makes an object on the heap and returns a pointer (delete it when done)
nullptr: A pointer that points to nothing
reinterpret_cast: Reads the contents of memory as a different type (a dangerous conversion; used when touching hardware)
try: Wraps code where an exception may occur
catch: Receives an exception thrown inside try
invalid_argument: The exception class for when an argument is wrong
endl: Ends the line and sends the output right away
ostream: The type of an output stream (such as cout)
printf: Shows text in a set format (%d is an integer, %f a decimal, %s a string)
vector: An array whose length can change (std::vector<int> and so on)
map: Key–value pairs (std::map). Kept in key order
push_back: Adds to the end of a vector
strlen: The length of a C string
strcmp: Compares C strings (0 if they are the same)
memset: Fills memory with a given value
fabs: The absolute value of a decimal
make_unique: Makes a unique_ptr (a pointer that is deleted automatically when done)
unique_ptr: A smart pointer with only one owner. Deleted automatically when no longer used
optional: A type expressing whether there is a value or not (std::optional)
size_t: An unsigned integer type for sizes and counts
sleep_for: Waits for a set length of time
greater: A comparison for sorting largest first (std::greater<int>())
